taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-13, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1340.2 | 1.08 | 1.08
2 | 2148.3 | 1.38 | 2.46
3 | 5322.7 | 1.26 | 3.72
4 | 18475.7 | 0.33 | 4.05
5 | 19320.3 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AKH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-13, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station T-13, Survey Area T**

The VES interpretation at T-13 resolves five layers with resistivities increasing monotonically with depth: 1340.2 Ω·m (0–1.08 m), 2148.3 Ω·m (1.08–2.46 m), 5322.7 Ω·m (2.46–3.72 m), 18475.7 Ω·m (3.72–4.05 m), and 19320.3 Ω·m (basal layer, no lower boundary resolved). This steady upward trend in resistivity suggests a transition from near-surface weathered/overburden material into increasingly resistive, likely more competent or drier substrate at depth, with no indication of a low-resistivity (conductive) layer such as clay or saturated zone within the sounded interval.

Applying the standard curve-type convention to the three consecutive-layer triplets yields A, A, A (since each triplet satisfies r1 < r2 < r3), i.e., curve type **A** (AAA). This does not match the on-file classification of "AKH," which implies a decrease in resistivity at some point (K requires a resistivity high followed by a drop; H requires a low between two highs) — neither feature is present in this monotonically increasing dataset. The file classification should be corrected to A-type.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKH", "label_issue_flagged": true}
